claims.text: Adding a reactive dopant will enable CoCrFeNi to maintain low friction and reduced wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy has a uniform microstructure.
The starting CoCrFeNi alloy contains no preformed self-lubricating phase.
The reactive dopant remains benign at low temperatures.
Under high-temperature sliding, the dopant diffuses and oxidizes.
The reactive dopant induces nanoscale precipitates or in situ tribofilms at the sliding interface.
At lower temperatures, the dopant remains dissolved in the alloy.
A dissolved dopant preserves the baseline properties of CoCrFeNi at lower temperatures.
Increasing temperature drives the dopant toward the sliding interface.
The dopant reacts at the interface to form a stable, lubricious film.
The lubricious film reduces interfacial shear stress and thereby lowers friction and wear.
Comparable dopant-generated lubricious-film behavior has been reported in other self-lubricating systems.
The doped alloy will have lower coefficient of friction than undoped CoCrFeNi throughout the entire room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The doped alloy will have lower wear rate than undoped CoCrFeNi throughout the entire room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The dopant's tribological benefits will be greatest near 800 °C.
Friction in undoped CoCrFeNi increases with temperature because lattice disorder increases.
Wear in undoped CoCrFeNi increases with temperature.
Oxide-induced degradation contributes to increasing friction and wear in undoped CoCrFeNi.
The intervention is effective from room temperature to 800 °C under moderate loads in air.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says that the dopant remains dissolved and merely preserves baseline properties at lower temperatures, while the predicted outcome requires lower friction and wear than the baseline over the entire range, including those lower temperatures. No low-temperature mediator is supplied to explain that improvement.
